html:
The Jaqaru are a small Indigenous people of Yauyos Province in the Lima Region of Peru, centred on the villages of Tupe and Catahuasi high in the Andes. About 2,000 people are Jaqaru, and many have moved to Lima.

Their language is the closest living relative of Aymara and the main evidence that Aymaran languages were once spoken across central Peru before Quechua spread. A related dialect, Kawki, is spoken in a nearby village. Tupe women are known for their red and black checked dress. See also the Aymara lordships of the south.
